findings.body:
**Inventory reports a different blocked reason for `blocked-secret-scan` receipts than `status` does.**

`status` and `inventory` give different reasons for the same receipt:

- At Line 672-673, `handle` maps a receipt with `outcome == "blocked-secret-scan"` to `{"source": "queue", "category": "scan", "code": "blocked-secret-scan"}`.
- In `_inventory`, the same receipt falls through to the `else` branch at Line 285-287. That branch returns `{"source": "queue", "category": "unknown", "code": "unclassified"}`.

The module docstring says inventory filtering and proof use the same row facts as status. Here, `inventory` and `status` disagree on the `reason` for the same `requestId` and receipt. A client that triages through `inventory` sees an unclassified failure. A client that triages through `status` sees a scan block. Add the same scan branch to `_inventory`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
                 elif doc.get("outcome") in {"no-current-code", "partial-scope"}:
                     row["state"] = doc["outcome"]
+                elif doc.get("outcome") == "blocked-secret-scan":
+                    row.update(state="blocked", reason={"source": "queue", "category": "scan", "code": "blocked-secret-scan"})
                 else:
                     row.update(state="blocked", reason={"source": "vendor", "category": "vendor-rate-limited", "code": "rate_limit"}
                                if _vendor_rate_limit(doc) else {"source": "queue", "category": "unknown", "code": "unclassified"})
```
</details>
findings.title: Inventory reports a different blocked reason for `blocked-secret-scan` receipts than `status` does.

findings.body:
**`discover()` calls `discover_merged` without the required `interval` argument.**

`discover_merged` declares `interval` as a required keyword-only parameter. The `discover()` helper omits it, so Python raises `TypeError` while binding arguments, before the function body runs. Any call to `self.discover()` errors before its assertions execute.

The other `discover_merged` calls in this test class pass `interval` explicitly. Pass the same frozen interval from the helper:

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     def discover(self, q=None):
-        return crq.discover_merged(self.q if q is None else q, crq.ForgeBudget())
+        return crq.discover_merged(self.q if q is None else q, crq.ForgeBudget(),
+                                   interval={"after": self.AFTER, "before": self.BEFORE})
```

</details>
findings.title: `discover()` calls `discovermerged` without the required `interval` argument.

findings.body:
**Classify `blocked-secret-scan` receipts as `scan` in `_inventory`, as `status` does.**

For a receipt with `outcome == "blocked-secret-scan"`, `status` sets the reason to `{"source": "queue", "category": "scan", "code": "blocked-secret-scan"}` (`queue_transport.py:672-673`). `_inventory` has no branch for that outcome. The row falls through to the `else` at `queue_transport.py:285-287`, which sets `unclassified`. The same receipt therefore gets different blocked reasons from `inventory` and `status`.

Add the scan branch before the vendor and unclassified fallback. This order matches `status`, where the scan reason overrides the vendor check.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
                 elif doc.get("outcome") in {"no-current-code", "partial-scope"}:
                     row["state"] = doc["outcome"]
+                elif doc.get("outcome") == "blocked-secret-scan":
+                    row.update(state="blocked", reason={"source": "queue", "category": "scan", "code": "blocked-secret-scan"})
                 else:
                     row.update(state="blocked", reason={"source": "vendor", "category": "vendor-rate-limited", "code": "rate_limit"}
                                if _vendor_rate_limit(doc) else {"source": "queue", "category": "unknown", "code": "unclassified"})
```

</details>
findings.title: Classify `blocked-secret-scan` receipts as `scan` in `inventory`, as `status` does.
